answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils the way a remote island guards its lagoon: entry requires one unique public-good contribution — a dataset, tool, or analysis no other identity has ever published. Peers review each artifact for originality and real utility, and its hash is bound to the identity forever, like onyx set in stone. A Sybil farmer must produce skilled work for every fake identity, since copying an artifact fails similarity checks and forfeits the entry bond. Open admission stays, but each identity costs irreplaceable labor and patience.
